緒.meaning: <part>Someone</part> on the beach breaks a sandal, so they twist strong <part>thread</part> into a cord and loop it between their toes to hold the sole on. It works! Now it has a <kanji>thong</kanji>, the strap of a sandal.
緒.on: They hop to the beach <sound>sho</sound>p for a new pair, but it's closed.
緒.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' they sigh, as the cord snaps again.

寂.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of a huge empty house lives an old <part>uncle</part>. All the cousins have moved away, so he sets the table for one, chats to the clock and waves at the postman twice. Every room echoes. He's full of <kanji>loneliness</kanji>.
寂.on: So he buys a <sound>jacu</sound>zzi big enough for twenty and sits in it all alone, bubbling.
寂.kun: He shares his supper with a single <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>bee</sound> on the windowsill.

避.meaning: A thief races down the <part>ramp</part> into the market with the police close behind. At the last second he dives under a <part>chili stall</part>, and they run straight past, sneezing. He got away! He managed to <kanji>evade</kanji> them.
避.on: Then he slips on a chili and snaps the <sound>hee</sound>l off his shoe.
避.kun: He tiptoes off, ducking a <sound>sa</sound>rdine that flies from the fish stall.

海.meaning: <part>Every</part> one of the <part>water drops</part> that fall on the hills packs a tiny suitcase and sets off downhill: down the gutter, along a stream, over a waterfall. Splash! They all meet again in one huge, salty, wavy place. They've reached the <kanji>sea</kanji>.
海.on: On the beach, a boy flies a <sound>ki</sound>te shaped like a whale.
海.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, seeing the waves for the very first time.

舟.meaning: Look at the shape: a long frame with two dots inside, like two people sitting, and a bar across it for the oar. Two friends paddle it over a lake, splashing and arguing about whose turn it is to row. It's a little <kanji>boat</kanji>.
舟.on: When it springs a leak, they bail it out with a giant <sound>shoe</sound>.
舟.kun: They nap on a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the bottom and catch fish in a <sound>ne</sound>t.

航.meaning: A <part>boat</part> has lost its compass, so the captain sets a <part>cake stand</part> on deck with a candle on top and steers by the way the flame leans. Left at the lighthouse, right at the rocks, all the way home. That's how she can <kanji>navigate</kanji>.
航.on: To mark the route, she drops an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne overboard at every turn.
